title: Bencao Dian — Open Data v1
description: Schema overview for the Bencao Dian seed dataset. The authoritative TypeScript types are in src/lib/data/types.ts in the source repository.

files.description: Herb entries — nature, flavor, channel entry, actions, indications, processing, dosage, contraindications, classical citations, Wikidata cross-references.
Formula entries — sovereign-minister-assistant-courier composition, modifications, treatment principle, source text.
Pattern entries — cardinal and secondary symptoms, tongue and pulse, etiology, pathomechanism, treatment principle.
Meridian entries — the twelve regular channels plus the Conception and Governing Vessels.
Acupoint entries — location, needling depth and method, special-category memberships, actions, indications.
Classical text entries — author, dynasty, tradition, annotated source passages.
Concept essays — yin-yang, five phases, zang-fu, eight principles, four natures and five flavors, sovereign-minister-assistant-courier hierarchy, and other foundational theory.
The relationship graph — herb_in_formula, formula_treats_pattern, pattern_differential_with, and ten other edge types.
Classical 医案 case records — famous historical cases from Ye Tianshi, Wu Jutong, Shanghan Lun, and other masters.
Tongue atlas — tongue body, shape, coating, clinical significance, with hand-authored SVG paths.
28 classical pulses — classical descriptions, modern descriptions, and clinical significance.
Symptom synonym ontology — 155 canonical symptoms each with ZH + EN aliases, powering symptom search and pattern differentiation.
Herb–drug interaction dataset — mechanism, clinical recommendation, and source citation.
Modern-condition index — cross-framework lookup from biomedical diagnosis to TCM pattern.

common_fields.key: Stable identifier (snake_case). Never changes after publication.
common_fields.slug: URL segment (kebab-case). Never changes after publication.
common_fields.name_zh: Chinese name (simplified or traditional, as appropriate).
common_fields.wikidata_id: Wikidata Q-identifier where a confident species or text mapping exists.

verification.reviewer: 'Bencaodian Editorial / 本草典编辑部' or named reviewer
